title: Fish motif
subtitle: A flat applique fish with a fan tail and scale texture, 10 cm
excerpt: The fish motif builds an oval body in dc rows with a five-treble fan tail at the wide end and a small embroidered eye. The body is worked in the round in a single oval, giving a clean edge for applique. At 10 cm long in DK cotton it is suitable for children's blankets, beach bag decoration, and bathroom textiles.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from flat oval applique and fan construction. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 8 (1893), flat animal applique chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A crochet fish applique in teal DK cotton with a five-treble fan tail and orange embroidered eye, 10 cm long, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. Clean oval body, wide tail fan clearly visible.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished fish motif measures 10 cm long and 5 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Fish motif
chartDefinition.caption: Oval body worked in the round from a chain foundation. Fan tail of 5tr at the wide end worked into the final border. Embroidered eye and fin line.

glossaryTerms.definition: Working in the round from a chain, with stitches along both sides of the chain and increases at each end to produce an oval rather than a circle.

content.text: for the body: a chain worked along both sides in the round, with 3-dc increases at each rounded end to keep the oval flat. Two rounds give a solid body. The fan tail is added as five trebles into the same space at the wider end, then a second fan ch-1 apart to form a two-lobe tail. An embroidered eye and a chain line for the pectoral fin complete the fish.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 10 g of DK cotton for the body, 3 g for the tail if contrast. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Embroidery thread for eye. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished fish motif measures 10 cm long and 5 cm tall in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
shell (5tr in same sp) — fan shell for the tail.

Ch 14. Rnd 1: Dc in 2nd ch from hook. Dc in next 10 ch. 3dc in last ch (round end). Working along the underside of the foundation chain: dc in next 10 ch. 2dc in first ch (other round end). Sl st to first dc. (30 dc.) Rnd 2: Ch 1. Dc in each dc around, working 2dc into each of the 3 corner stitches at the wide end. Sl st to first dc. (About 36 dc.) Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail.

Join tail colour (or same colour) to the centre dc at the narrow (tail) end of the body. Work 5tr all into the same stitch. Ch 1. Join to the next dc and work another 5tr fan all into that stitch. Sl st to anchor. Fasten off.

definition.title: Fish motif
definition.caption: Oval body: ch-14 foundation, dc along both sides with 3dc at wide end, two rounds. Two 5tr fan shells at narrow tail end.

content.text: Embroider a French knot eye near the wide head end. Add a chain line for the pectoral fin if desired. Sew the fish onto the base fabric through the body border.
Handwash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.

The fox motif (crochet-animal-fox) uses a similar oval body construction with a pointed ear and tail extension. The lotus motif (crochet-flower-lotus) uses the same fan-shell construction as the fish tail for flower petals.
